newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso steady on industrial data, long bond.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso steady on industrial data, long bond.

text.p: The Mexican peso retained most of its initial gains in late morning trade on Thursday due to a continuing slide in U.S. long bond yields.
Dealers said the peso was testing firm resistance at 7.7600 per dollar, which had prevented the peso gathering further strength, despite strong industrial output data.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart were trading 1.05 and 1.5 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.7665/7.7685 and 7.7580/7.7620 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had, meanwhile, closed trade for the day 1.95 centavos firmer at 7.7560/7.7595 per dollar.
"The data are definitely good for Mexico and the peso, but even so I don't expect it to break through the 7.86 per dollar mark," a trader said.

The Financial Ministry announced Mexico's industrial output in June increased by 9.9 percent from year-ago figures. A previously conducted Reuters survey had forecast an average increase of 8.3 percent.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds had meanwhile stretched an early advance and were up 24/32 to yield 6.57 percent.
